note.subject: biology
note.title: Aseptic reasoning
note.overview: Interpret controls, contamination and risk assessment in the supervised school culture practical.
learningGoals: Explain the key idea using school examples.
Apply it to a short-answer or calculation question.
mustMemoriseRules: Aseptic technique reduces unwanted contamination and exposure.
A sterile-water negative control should have no growth; growth suggests contamination.
Label the base, keep the dish open as little as possible, invert it to prevent condensation dripping and follow the teacher’s containment rules.
An autoclave uses pressurised steam to sterilise equipment and waste.
detailedExplanation: Aseptic technique reduces unwanted contamination and exposure.
A sterile-water negative control should have no growth; growth suggests contamination.
Label the base, keep the dish open as little as possible, invert it to prevent condensation dripping and follow the teacher’s containment rules.
An autoclave uses pressurised steam to sterilise equipment and waste.

workedExamples.answer: Hazard: flame. Risk: burn. Control: follow the teacher’s safe positioning and supervision.
workedExamples.why: Follow the units and the biological reason given in the explanation.

commonMistakes: A hazard is a source of harm, while a risk is the possible harm and its likelihood.
Interpret any growth on a negative control as a warning about validity.
